english: Concerning the need, according to the church's canon, that those who have freely and lawfully entered second marriages, and have not made a secret marriage, after a little time has passed and they have devoted themselves to prayers and fasts, are by concession to have communion given back to them—this we decreed.

Interpretation. The present canon determines that those who marry a second time are to partake of the divine mysteries after a little time, by concession, because of the necessity and burning of nature, provided only that their second marriage is free and lawful, that is, not impeded by any kinship. But if they sleep together before being blessed, and if after the marriage they repent, fasting and praying—Basil's fourth canon bars the twice-married from communion for one year or two, and it appears that this synod grants the twice-married communion in a little time because of their fasting and prayer, and simply put, because of their repentance. On this read the twelfth canon of the first synod. See also the seventh canon of the synod at Ancyra. But if these twice-married persons have intercourse before the marriage, they are to be punished as fornicators, according to Zonaras, that is, for seven years.
title: Second marriages and communion after a short time
orientation: The Council of Laodicea opens with a canon on admitting those who have entered a lawful second marriage to communion after a short period of repentance.

english: Concerning those who sin in various ways and persist in the prayer of confession and repentance, and who make a complete turning away from evils: after a time of repentance has been given to such persons in proportion to their offense, they are to be brought to communion because of the mercies and the goodness of God.

Interpretation. This present canon decrees that even if someone falls into various sins, but confesses them and turns away from them and hates them, praying and repenting before God—such a person, once a time of repentance and satisfaction has been given to him by the Spiritual Father, proportionate to the evils he has done, must be forgiven and receive the divine Mysteries. This is not because of his own diligence or worthiness, but because of the infinite love for humanity and the mercies of God, who receives all who turn back to him, and no sin overcomes his goodness. See also canon 12 of the first council.
title: Reconciling repentant sinners to communion
orientation: The council is decreeing how sinners who repent and persist in prayer are to be brought back to communion.

english: Concerning the rule that one recently baptized must not be brought forward into the priestly order. Interpretation. This present canon commands that the newly baptized must not become Priests or Clerics immediately after the baptism. See also Apostolic Canon 80.
title: The newly baptized must not be ordained at once
orientation: The council is issuing its canons; this one addresses who may be brought into the clerical order.

english: Concerning the rule that clergy must not lend money, charge interest, or take what are called one-and-a-half rates. Interpretation. According to this present canon, clergy must not lend money and take interest and one-and-a-half rates—that is, half of the whole rate on a hundred, meaning six coins or piasters per hundred. See also Apostolic Canon 44.
title: Clergy must not lend at interest
orientation: The council is issuing a canon forbidding clergy from lending money at interest, followed by an interpretation explaining the rates.

english: Concerning the requirement that ordinations not take place in the presence of hearers. Interpretation. The present Canon decrees that the ordinations of the clergy must not take place in front of hearers. See also Apostolic Canons 30 and 61.
title: Ordinations must not be held in the presence of hearers
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its canons; this section is a heading and interpretation of Canon 5, which forbids ordinations from taking place before hearers.

english: Concerning the rule that heretics are not to be permitted to enter the house of God while persisting in the heresy. Interpretation. The decree of the present Canon is that heretics are not to have permission to enter the temple of God, the one held by orthodox, if they persist in the heresy and do not wish to return. See also Apostolic Canon 45.
title: Heretics barred from the church building while persisting in heresy
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its sixth canon, now forbidding heretics who persist in their heresy from entering the church building held by the orthodox.

english: Concerning those from the heresies—that is, Novatians, Photinians, or Quartodecimans—who are returning, whether catechumens or faithful among those people: they are not to be received until they anathematize every heresy, and especially the one in which they were held. Then, after that, those called faithful among them, once they have learned thoroughly the symbols of the faith and have been anointed with the holy chrism, may share in the holy mysteries.

Interpretation. Following canon 7 of the Second Council, the present canon also decrees that Novatians (concerning whom see canon 8 of the First Council), Photinians (concerning whom see canon 1 of the Second Council), and Quartodecimans (concerning whom see canon 7 of the Second Council) who are returning to orthodoxy are not to be received into the communion of the mysteries before they anathematize every other heresy, and especially their own, whether they are catechumens or those called faithful among them. And after they do this and learn the doctrines of the orthodox faith, then they are to be anointed with the holy chrism, and in this way they are to partake of the divine mysteries, since they were baptized in exactly the same manner as the orthodox, and for this reason they did not need to be baptized a second time. See also Apostolic Canons 46 and 47, and especially canon 7 of the Second Council.
title: Reception of returning Novatians, Photinians, and Quartodecimans
orientation: The Council of Laodicea decrees how heretics from three named sects are to be received back into the church.

english: Concerning those returning from the heresy of the so-called Phrygians: even if they happen to be in a clergy deemed such among them, even if they are called the greatest, such persons are to be catechized and baptized with all care by the bishops and presbyters of the church.

This canon also agrees with canon 7 of the Second Council. For it decrees, as that one does, that the so-called Phrygians, that is, the Montanists, when they return to orthodoxy, must be catechized and baptized as Greeks by the bishops and presbyters, with examination and care—even if they themselves are called the greatest, as teachers and those surpassing the others, and even if they are from those deemed among them, but not truly being, clerics. Read also Apostolic Canons 46 and 47, and especially canon 7 of the Second Council.
title: Reception of returning Phrygians requires catechesis and baptism
orientation: The council continues its rulings on how heretics returning to orthodoxy are to be received, now addressing the Phrygians (Montanists).

english: Those who belong to the church must not go to the cemeteries or the so-called martyria of any heretics for prayer or for healing. If any of the faithful do so, they are to become excommunicated until a certain time. But if they repent and confess that they have erred, they are to be received back.

Interpretation. Not only must heretics not enter the churches of the orthodox, but neither should those of the church—that is, the faithful laity and orthodox—go to the cemeteries of heretics, where certain persons famous among the heretics have been buried, or to the houses where martyrs of the heretics were buried. For many of the heretics also endured to the death in the time of persecution and idolatry, and their fellow-believers called them martyrs. But neither, I say, should orthodox Christians go to them either to pray or for healing—that is, either to honor them or to seek a cure from them for their illnesses. Whoever does this, the present canon decrees, is to be excommunicated for a time, until they repent and confess that they have erred. See also Apostolic Canon 45.
title: No visiting heretics' shrines
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is decreeing that church members must not go to the burial places or martyrs' shrines of heretics for prayer or healing, and that those who do so are to be excommunicated for a time.

english: Concerning the rule that members of the church must not join their children in the communion of marriage with heretics indiscriminately. Interpretation: Those of the church—that is, clergy as well as orthodox laity—must not marry off their children to heretics without making any distinction between orthodox and heretic. Read also canon 14 of the Fourth.
title: No indiscriminate marriage of church children to heretics
orientation: The council is issuing its tenth canon, now forbidding members of the church from marrying their children to heretics without distinction.

english: Concerning the rule that the so-called eldresses, that is, presidents, must not be appointed in the church. Interpretation: Zonaras and Balsamon say that this canon decrees that the women called old women and presidents over the rest must not be made in the church, nor even be called by such a name, because in ancient times there were such old women in the churches who put the other women in order—how and where each one should stand and sit in the temple. Since they used this work for shameful gain and pride, the canon prevented them from it. Others say that the canon prevents these eldresses and presidents from being appointed, that is, from being ordained through prayers, since "to be appointed" also means "to be ordained through prayers," as we said in the fourth canon of the first council.
title: No women elders or presidents in the church
orientation: The council is giving its canon against appointing the women called elders or presidents in the church, followed by the Byzantine commentators' interpretation of that canon.

english: Concerning the appointment of bishops to the ecclesiastical office by the judgment of the metropolitans and the surrounding bishops, they being long since tested both in the word of faith and in the conduct of upright life.

Interpretation. The present canon decrees that those being ordained bishops are to be made so by the judgment and vote of the surrounding metropolitans and bishops of the province, they having been tested and witnessed for many years beforehand, both according to the orthodox doctrines of the faith and according to the virtuous conduct that comes about with right reason. See also Apostolic Canon 1 and Canon 4 of the First Council.
title: Bishops appointed by metropolitan judgment after long testing
orientation: The council is decreeing how bishops are to be appointed to ecclesiastical office, requiring the judgment of the metropolitan and neighboring bishops and prior testing in faith and upright life.

english: Concerning not permitting the crowds to hold elections for those who are to be appointed to the priesthood. This canon forbids the crowds and the disorderly multitudes of the cities from casting votes and holding elections for those who are about to be ordained as priests (or even as bishops). First, because by the primary argument such men must be voted on by the High Priests and their fellow priests, and subsequently the people should join in the vote as well. Second, because perhaps the wiser and more devout laity ought to vote together with the bishops and priests for the man who is to be ordained as their priest (or even as bishop), but not the vulgar and disorderly mob, on account of the quarrels and fights that can arise in their voting, when some vote for one man and others for another. See also the note on canon 5 of this council, and Apostolic Canons 30 and 61.
title: Elections to the priesthood must not be left to the crowds
orientation: The council is giving its own rule, with an attached explanation, that the disorderly crowds of the cities must not make the elections of those about to be ordained priests or high priests.

english: Concerning the holy things not being sent across to other parishes by way of blessings at the feast of Pascha. Interpretation. It was a custom among the ancients to send the divine Mysteries at the time of Pascha from one province to another, for the blessing and sanctification of those to whom they were sent. This custom the present canon hinders, because it is improper for the all-honored Mysteries to be carried about on long journeys simply and as it happened.
title: No sending the holy gifts as blessings at Pascha
orientation: The council is issuing its canons; this one forbids a custom of sending the consecrated eucharistic gifts from one parish to another at Pascha as a blessing.

english: Concerning the rule that no one except the canonical singers, who go up onto the ambo and chant from parchment, may sing in church. Interpretation. The present canon hinders just anyone from singing in the church; only the canonical singers may do so—that is, those who are enrolled in the clergy and ordained in each church. These go up onto the ambo and chant from parchment sheets (for diphtherai is the name for the skins from which parchment sheets are made), or from paper ones. For disorder and discordant noise follow if some untrained person happens to sing, and on the contrary good order follows when the appointed singers, experienced in chanting, do the singing. See also canon 75 of the Sixth Council.
title: Only canonical singers may chant in church
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its canons; this canon regulates who may chant in church, and the source includes the canon heading, the canon text, and a later Greek interpretation.

english: That on the Sabbath the gospels are to be read together with the other Scriptures.
title: Saturday Gospel with other Scriptures
orientation: The council is issuing a canon about the order of readings in the Saturday liturgy.

english: Psalms are not to be joined together one after another in the assemblies. Instead, a reading is to take place through the middle, after each psalm.
title: Psalms must be separated by readings
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon regulates how psalms are to be performed in the assemblies.

english: The same liturgy of the prayers ought always to take place at the ninth hours and at the evening hours.
title: Same liturgy of prayers at the ninth hour and at vespers
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon regulates the daily prayer services.

english: After the homilies of the bishops, the prayer for the catechumens should first be offered separately. After the catechumens have gone out, the prayer for those in repentance should take place. When these have come forward under the hand and withdrawn, then the prayers of the faithful should be offered—three of them: the first completed in silence, the second and third through spoken address. Then the peace should be given. After the presbyters have given the peace to the bishop, then the laity should exchange the peace, and so the holy offering should be completed. And only the priestly ones may enter the sanctuary and receive communion.
title: Order of prayers and the offering
orientation: The council is legislating the sequence of the liturgy: separate prayers for catechumens, penitents, and faithful, then the kiss of peace and the offering.

english: A deacon must not sit in front of a presbyter, but may sit only with the presbyter's permission. Likewise, the deacons should receive honor from the servants and from all the clergy.
title: Deacons' seating and honor
orientation: The council is issuing a rule about the seating order and honor of deacons relative to presbyters and other clergy.

english: Servants are not to be stationed in the diaconicon or to touch the sacred vessels.
title: Servants must not handle sacred vessels
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon restricts the role of servants in the sanctuary.

english: A servant is not to wear the deacon's stole, nor abandon the doors.
title: Servants must not wear the deacon's stole or abandon the doors
orientation: The council continues its rules on the lower clergy, now forbidding servants from wearing the deacon's stole or leaving their post at the doors.

english: Readers and singers are not to wear the deacon's stole and read or chant while wearing it.
title: Readers and singers must not wear the deacon's stole
orientation: The council continues its rules on liturgical order, now addressing readers and singers.

english: No cleric, from presbyters as far as deacons and on through the ecclesiastical rank down to servants, readers, singers, exorcists, doorkeepers, or the order of ascetics, is to enter into a tavern.
title: Clergy and church orders barred from taverns
orientation: The council is issuing a series of disciplinary canons; this one forbids all ranks of clergy and church orders from entering a tavern.

english: A servant is not permitted to give the bread or to bless the cup.
title: Servants may not distribute bread or bless the cup
orientation: The council is issuing a short disciplinary canon about liturgical roles, after the opening of the canons.

english: Those who have not been appointed by bishops are not permitted to exorcize, either in the churches or in private homes.
title: Exorcism only by those appointed by bishops
orientation: The council is issuing a canon about who may perform exorcisms.

english: Priests, clergy, or lay people who are invited to a love feast must not take portions away with them, because this brings insult upon the order of the church.
title: No taking portions at a love feast
orientation: The council continues its rules on church order, now forbidding clergy and laity invited to a love feast from taking portions.

english: One must not hold the so-called love feasts on the Lord's days or in churches, nor eat in the house of God, nor spread dining couches.
title: No love feasts in church buildings
orientation: The council continues its rules on love feasts, now forbidding them inside church buildings.

english: Christians must not Judaize or be idle on the Sabbath, but must work on that day. They should prefer the Lord's day and, if they are able, rest on it as Christians. But if any are found to be Judaizers, let them be accursed before Christ.
title: Christians must not Judaize or keep the Sabbath
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon forbids Christians from observing the Jewish Sabbath.

english: Priestly men, clerics, or ascetics must not bathe in a bathhouse with women, nor may any Christian or layman do so. For this is the first condemnation among the pagans.
title: No bathing with women for clergy or Christians
orientation: The council continues issuing prohibitions, now forbidding clergy, ascetics, and all Christians from bathing with women.

english: Christians must not make marriage alliances with any heretics, giving them sons or daughters in marriage. Rather, they should receive them in marriage, if indeed those heretics promise to become Christians.
title: No marriage alliances with heretics
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon forbids Christians from giving their children in marriage to heretics.

english: Christians must not receive blessings from heretics, for these are not blessings at all but rather non-blessings.
title: Heretics' blessings are not blessings
orientation: The council continues its rules on avoiding heretics, now forbidding Christians to receive blessings from them.

english: It is not right to pray together with heretics or schismatics.
title: No praying with heretics or schismatics
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon forbids Christians from praying together with heretics or schismatics.

english: No Christian should abandon the martyrs of Christ and turn to false martyrs. These are the martyrs of heretics, or those who have themselves joined those same heretics. They are strangers to God. Let anyone who goes to them be accursed.
title: No visiting the false martyrs of heretics
orientation: The council continues forbidding contact with heretics by regulating whose martyrs Christians may visit.

english: Christians must not abandon the church of God and go away to invoke angels and hold assemblies, which has been forbidden. If anyone is found devoting himself to this hidden idolatry, let him be accursed, because he has abandoned our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and gone over to idolatry.
title: Against secret idolatry and angel assemblies
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its decrees; this canon forbids Christians from leaving the church to name angels and hold assemblies, and curses anyone found practicing such hidden idolatry.

english: Priests or clergy must not be magicians or enchanters, or stargazers, or astrologers, or make what are called amulets, which are prisons of their souls. We have commanded that those who wear them be thrown out of the church.
title: Clergy must not practice magic or make amulets
orientation: The council continues its decrees against idolatry, now forbidding clergy from magical arts and ordering those who wear amulets to be cast out of the church.

english: It is not right to receive festal things sent by Jews or heretics, nor to celebrate together with them.
title: No receiving festival gifts from Jews or heretics
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon forbids Christians from accepting festive gifts sent by Jews or heretics or celebrating together with them.

english: It is not right to take unleavened bread from the Jews, or to share in their impieties.
title: No unleavened bread or fellowship with Jewish impiety
orientation: The council continues its rulings against sharing in Jewish religious practices, now forbidding Christians to take unleavened bread from Jews or to share in their impiety.

english: It is not right to celebrate festivals together with pagans, or to share in their godlessness.
title: No shared festivals with pagans
orientation: The council continues its rules against sharing in non-Christian religious life, now addressing pagan festivals.

english: Bishops who are called to a synod must not despise the summons. They are to go, and to teach or be taught, for the correction of the church and of the rest. If such a bishop despises the summons, he will blame himself—unless he is prevented by illness.
title: Bishops must not despise a synod summons
orientation: The council is issuing its own decrees, and this canon addresses bishops who are called to a synod.

english: A priestly person or a cleric is not permitted to travel without the order of the bishop.
title: No travel without the bishop's order
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon restricts travel by clergy.

english: Priestly persons or clerics are not permitted to travel without canonical letters.
title: Priests and clerics need canonical letters to travel
orientation: The council is decreeing travel rules for clergy, continuing from the previous canon about not traveling without the bishop's order.

english: Servants must not abandon the doors, even briefly, to devote themselves to prayer.
title: Servants must not leave the doors
orientation: The council is issuing a rule about the conduct of servants during worship.

english: It is not right for women to enter the sanctuary.
title: Women must not enter the sanctuary
orientation: The council continues its rules for worship by forbidding women from entering the sanctuary.

english: No one is to be received into the baptism after two weeks of Lent.
title: No baptismal enrollment after the second week of Lent
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon sets a deadline for admitting candidates to baptism during Lent.

english: Those being baptized must learn the faith thoroughly, and on the fifth day of the week they are to report to the bishop or to the presbyters.
title: Catechumens must learn and recite the creed
orientation: The council is legislating baptismal preparation, just after limiting reception into baptism to before the last two weeks of Lent.

english: Those who receive the enlightenment while sick, and then rise up, must learn the faith thoroughly and know that they were deemed worthy of a divine gift.
title: Baptism in sickness still requires learning the faith
orientation: The council is legislating for those who receive baptism while ill and then recover.

english: Those being baptized must be anointed with heavenly chrism after baptism, and so become sharers in the kingdom of Christ.
title: Chrismation after baptism
orientation: The council is decreeing what must happen to those being baptized immediately after their baptism.

english: During Lent one must not to offer bread except on the Sabbath and the Lord's Day only.
title: Offering bread only on Sabbath and Lord's Day in Lent
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its canons, and this canon regulates when the Eucharistic offering of bread may be made during Lent.

english: It is not right to break the fast on the fifth day of the last week of Lent, and so dishonor the whole of Lent. Instead, one must fast throughout all of Lent, eating dry food.
title: Fasting the whole of Lent
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is decreeing how the Lenten fast must be kept, continuing from the previous canon about not offering bread except on Sabbath and the Lord's Day.

english: It is not right to celebrate the birthdays of martyrs during Lent. Instead, the commemorations of the holy martyrs should be made on the Sabbaths and on the Lord's days.
title: No martyr birthdays in Lent
orientation: The council is giving rules for Lenten observance, now forbidding the celebration of martyrs' birthdays during Lent.

english: It is not right to celebrate weddings or birthdays during Lent.
title: No weddings or birthdays in Lent
orientation: The Council of Laodicea continues its Lenten regulations, now forbidding weddings and birthday celebrations during the forty-day fast.

english: Christians who go to weddings must not dance or leap about, but are to dine or breakfast with dignity, as is fitting for Christians.
title: Christians must behave with dignity at wedding feasts
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees; this canon regulates how Christians conduct themselves when they attend wedding celebrations.

english: Priests or clergy must not watch spectacles at weddings or dinners; before the entertainers come in, they are to get up and withdraw.
title: Clergy must leave before entertainers perform at weddings or dinners
orientation: The council is giving rules for clergy conduct at social gatherings, continuing from its rule on how Christians should behave at weddings.

english: Priests or clergy must not hold banquets funded by a common contribution, and neither may lay people.
title: No shared-cost banquets for clergy or laity
orientation: The council is issuing a short disciplinary canon about banquets, following the previous canon on clergy leaving wedding and dinner entertainments.

english: Presbyters must not enter and sit in the sanctuary before the bishop enters; they are to enter with the bishop, unless the bishop is unwell or away from home.
title: Presbyters must not enter or sit in the sanctuary before the bishop
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing a rule about the order in which presbyters and the bishop enter the sanctuary.

english: Bishops are not to be appointed in villages and country districts, but circuit visitors instead. Those already appointed beforehand are to do nothing without the judgment of the bishop in the city. Likewise, presbyters are to do nothing without the judgment of the bishop.
title: No bishops in villages; circuit visitors instead
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon regulates rural church order.

english: Bishops or presbyters are not to make the offering in private houses.
title: No offerings in private houses
orientation: The council continues its decrees on liturgical order, now forbidding bishops and presbyters from celebrating the offering in private homes.

english: Private psalms must not be said in church, nor uncanonical books, but only the canonical books of the new and old covenant.
title: Only canonical Scripture in church
orientation: The council is giving a rule about what may be read or sung in church, just before it lists the canonical books.

english: The books that are to be read from the Old Covenant are these: first, Genesis of the world; second, Exodus from Egypt; third, Leviticus; fourth, Numbers; fifth, Deuteronomy; sixth, Joshua of Nave; seventh, Judges, Ruth; eighth, Esther; ninth, of Kingdoms first and second; tenth, of Kingdoms third and fourth; eleventh, Chronicles first and second; twelfth, Ezra-Nehemiah first and second; thirteenth, the Book of Psalms, 150; fourteenth, Proverbs of Solomon; fifteenth, Ecclesiastes; sixteenth, Song of Songs; seventeenth, Job; eighteenth, the Minor Prophets; nineteenth, Isaiah; twentieth, Jeremiah and Baruch, Lamentations and epistles; twenty-first, Ezekiel; twenty-second, Daniel. The books of the New Covenant are these: four Gospels, according to Matthew, according to Mark, according to Luke, according to John; the Acts of the Apostles; seven catholic epistles—one of James, two of Peter, three of John, one of Jude; fourteen epistles of Paul—one to the Romans, two to the Corinthians, one to the Galatians, one to the Ephesians, one to the Philippians, one to the Colossians, two to the Thessalonians, one to the Hebrews, two to Timothy, one to Titus, and one to Philemon.
title: The Canonical Books of the Old and New Testaments
orientation: The Council of Laodicea closes its canons by listing the books of the Old and New Testaments that are to be read in church.
